# Fixed surviving C guardian CPU adoption observations

Two separate, once-only N1-1 CPU cases observed one fixed C product each, with roles G guardian → C coordinator → H guard → W worker. The reviewed source A `822d918b89caebee857e4c926e760d328805adf7` was pushed and integrated through [PR44](https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev/pull/44), merge `36a0c891229976b75de073a41a0458aa061c3122`, before either host case. [Source documentation](https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev/blob/822d918b89caebee857e4c926e760d328805adf7/docs/frontier-v8-owned-c-guardian.md) defines the closed protocol. Outer Python, compiler and linker activity is additional to the four C roles.

| guard_loss | C392747 reaped H392748/raw9; G392746 observed W392749 change parent H→G, reaped W/raw9, then reaped C/exit0 after FINISH/ACK | G_H and G_W each one pidfd SIGKILL attempt, flags0/result0/errno0 |
| coordinator_loss | G393079 reaped C393080/exit23/raw5888, separately observed H393081 then W393082 adopted by G, reaped H/raw9 and W/raw9 | G_H and G_W each one pidfd SIGKILL attempt, flags0/result0/errno0 |

G observed its own child-subreaper GET0, SET1 and GET1 before forks. Each child independently reported GET0. Native READY W→H→C and ARM/ACK/EOF barriers preceded case actions; W EOF originated at H and was forwarded, H EOF originated at C. Coordinator loss first closed C_H and acknowledged before exit23. The guard-loss case left C as H's parent and sole reaper; G never claimed a G_H wait there. In coordinator loss, W remained parented by H during H adoption, and W adoption was separately observed after H exit/reap. Each actual signal consumed its lifetime attempt immediately before the syscall; both successful cases used the planned ledger, with no negative cleanup signals. The terminal reset SET0/GET0 followed exact known-role reaps and descriptor/time predicates. These are controlled-source returned facts, not whole-ancestry or continuous code authentication.

Five pidfds were separately opened after forks: G_C, G_H, G_W, C_H and H_W. Four managed descriptors reported one explicit close followed immediately by F_GETFD=-1/EBADF9. H_W belongs to the killed guard: only owner-death kernel teardown is described, with no explicit H_W close/EBADF observation. Private-pipe, product and inherited-standard-descriptor closures are separately recorded. Shared work/cleanup/terminal/guardian budgets were 5/8/10/12 seconds from one epoch, with child expiry at 14 seconds; self-expiry is not an observed recovery result.

Each case returned four compiler-stage, one link and one runtime command, all 0, normally reaped with no outer timeout/kill. Current symbolic system headers/signatures supplied SYS_pidfd_open, SYS_pidfd_send_signal and the subreaper prctl constants; returned values 434/424/37/36 were observed expressions, not guessed architecture/provider numbers. Runtime scalar and integer representation facts matched the compiler facts.
